description.text: UMB Financial Corporation (together with its consolidated subsidiaries, unless the context requires otherwise, the Company) is a financial holding company that is headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri. The Company provides banking services and asset servicing to its customers in the United States and around the globe. The Company was organized as a corporation under Missouri law in 1967 and is registered as a bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the BHCA) and a financial holding company under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999, as amended (the GLBA). The Company currently owns all of the outstanding stock of one national bank and several nonbank subsidiaries. On January 31, 2025, the Company acquired all of the outstanding stock of Heartland Financial USA, Inc., a Delaware corporation (HTLF), in an all-stock transaction, issuing a total of 23.6 million shares of the Company’s common stock and 4.6 million depositary shares, each representing a 1/400th interest in a share of the Company’s 7.00% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A (the Company’s preferred stock).

about.description_short: UMB Financial Corporation (Nasdaq: UMBF) is a financial services company headquartered in Kansas City, Mo. UMB offers commercial banking, which includes comprehensive deposit, lending, investment and retirement plan services; personal banking, which includes comprehensive deposit, lending, wealth management and financial planning services; and institutional banking, which includes asset servicing, corporate trust solutions, investment banking and healthcare services. UMB operates branches throughout Missouri, Arizona, California, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Illinois, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, Utah, and Wisconsin. As the company's reach continues to grow, it also serves business clients nationwide and institutional clients in several countries. For more information, visit UMB.com, UMB Blog, UMB Facebook and UMB LinkedIn.

analysis_md:
# UMBF — UMB Financial Corporation
v5 run, 2026-10-19. In scope (market cap $9.551B at $129.65, nasdaq_quote_api). **Finance sector — the OE/capex DCF fits banks poorly; confidence is low by rule, and the final tier is softened one notch from tier-by-numbers under the universal misfit rule — see Final verdict.**

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json, financials_history.csv, or the cited search results — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Kansas City bank holding company (UMB Bank, N.A.; SIC 6021 National Commercial Banks per fundamentals.json profile): Commercial Banking, Institutional Banking (fund administration and accounting, custody, corporate trust, and HSA/healthcare payment services) and Personal Banking. The balance sheet stepped up on January 31, 2025, when the all-stock acquisition of Heartland Financial USA, Inc. (HTLF) closed — the largest acquisition in the company's history, adding $16.1B in assets and $9.7B in loans and extending the footprint from 8 to 13 states (Q2 2026 earnings materials, via search results); systems and brand conversion completed in October 2025. Q2 2026 (release, via search results): revenue $778.0M (+12.9% YoY), net interest income $532.5M (+14.0% YoY), noninterest income $245.5M (+10.5% YoY), net income available to common shareholders $271,758,000 or $3.56 diluted GAAP EPS (operating EPS $3.57 vs $2.96 in Q2 2025; the release's +21.1% YoY is its net-operating-income growth figure — a clean combined-vs-combined comparison, both quarters post-close), NIM (FTE) 3.32%, return on average common equity 14.16%, operating ROTCE 20.3%, end-of-period loans $41.1B, deposits $59.8B at June 30, 2026, net charge-offs 16bp of average loans and nonperforming loans 31bp of total loans. The board declared a $0.50 quarterly dividend (+16.3%) payable October 1, 2026.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,026,693,000; capex $48,584,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $37,745,000 (ShareBasedCompensation, always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $940,364,000 = $12.76/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $12.76, latest FY OE total $940.4M).
- Maintenance version (financials_history.csv): $795,584,000 — below the conservative figure; for a bank both definitions are approximations (loan growth, the real "capex" of a bank, is an investing outflow neither captures), which is exactly the sector-mismatch caveat.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt as the engine computes it is −$7,297,744,000 (cash $7,771,973,000 minus LongTermDebt $474,229,000 — deposits, a bank's real funding, are not in this figure; see BIG_NET_CASH below). Balance sheet at FY2025 (financials_history.csv): assets $73,094,090,000; liabilities $65,400,522,000; equity $7,693,568,000.
- History shape (financials_history.csv): conservative OE/share was $9.83 in FY2021, $14.28 in FY2022, $8.83 in FY2023, $3.72 in FY2024 and $12.76 in FY2025, while diluted EPS (fundamentals.json) moved $7.24 / $8.86 / $7.18 / $8.99 / $9.29 over the same years — the OE series' volatility is OCF plumbing (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE), not earnings volatility.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $1,026,693,000 − prior YTD $648,407,000 + current YTD $710,530,000 = **TTM $1,088,816,000**
- Capex: FY $48,584,000 − prior YTD $23,427,000 + current YTD $22,978,000 = **TTM $48,135,000**
- SBC: FY $37,745,000 − prior YTD $20,709,000 + current YTD $22,774,000 = **TTM $39,810,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **76,422,437**
- **TTM OE total $1,000,871,000 → base OE/share $13.10** (base_source: ttm_json)
- Why this base, of the three candidates: the TTM window (July 2025–June 2026) is the first fully-combined twelve months — every leg is post-Heartland-close, and the share denominator is the combined company's count, so there is no merger timing mismatch of the HBAN kind. Cross-check: fundamentals.json puts TTM net income at $942,679,000 against the TTM OE total of $1,000,871,000 — the OCF base sits close to the earnings base on this window, unlike the gross bank artifacts seen elsewhere in this sweep (ALLY). The normalized median ($8.83/share) is rejected as the scored base: two of its three years are the pre-Heartland standalone bank and its median year is FY2023, with FY2024's OCF trough ($3.72/share) inside the set — see BASE_DIVERGENCE. The median-base variant is still recorded in the method range below, with its IRR and tier, per the standing TTM-discretion standard.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate, high quality for a regional bank
Justification: operating ROTCE 20.3% in Q2 2026 with a 48.14% operating efficiency ratio and return on average common equity of 14.16% (Q2 2026 release, via search results), and a filed ROE history (fundamentals.json) of 11.2% / 16.2% / 11.3% / 12.7% in FY2021–FY2024 (FY2025's 9.1% divides by a year-end equity balance swollen by the Heartland stock issuance). fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for a bank presentation (both null), so ROE/ROTCE are the return evidence. Capped at moderate because the core product is commodity banking with no structural pricing power, the enlarged loan book is untested through a credit cycle, and returns now depend on holding Heartland's deposits after the October 2025 conversion.
- FOR:
  - Institutional Banking fee franchise — fund administration/accounting, custody and HSA/healthcare payment services are sticky, fee-rich and less capital-intensive than lending; noninterest income was $245.5M in Q2 2026, +10.5% YoY (Q2 2026 release)
  - Deposit franchise at scale — deposits $59.8B at June 30, 2026 against loans of $41.1B (a conservative loan-to-deposit posture), funding the balance sheet cheaply enough for a 3.32% FTE NIM
  - Best-in-class efficiency for a regional — operating efficiency ratio 48.14% in Q2 2026 (GAAP 48.35%), well ahead of large-regional peers, with operating ROTCE of 20.3% in the quarter
  - Asset quality and underwriting record — net charge-offs 16bp of average loans and nonperforming loans 31bp of total loans in Q2 2026; OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years
  - Heartland step-up delivered so far — acquisition closed January 31, 2025, systems/brand conversion completed October 2025, and Q2 2026 operating EPS of $3.57 (net operating income +21.1% YoY per the release) on a clean combined-vs-combined comparison
- AGAINST:
  - Commodity product, no structural pricing power — deposits and loans are fungible; NIM and deposit pricing are set by money-center banks, regionals and money-market alternatives
  - Credit-cycle exposure on an enlarged, unseasoned book — loans $41.1B at June 30, 2026 after the Heartland step-up, assembled in a benign stretch (charge-offs 16bp are a trough print, not a through-cycle level); FY2025 provision for credit losses was $154.5M even in a good year
  - Purchase-accounting accretion is a fading tailwind inside current earnings — the FY2025 cash-flow reconciliation shows net accretion of premiums/discounts from acquisition of $139,775,000 boosting FY2025 results
  - Capital-constrained growth — loan growth, the raised $0.50 quarterly dividend (+16.3%, declared for October 1, 2026) and any buybacks compete for the same regulatory capital
  - Rate sensitivity — earnings lean on NIM (net interest income $532.5M in Q2 2026, +14.0% YoY) and on lumpy private-investment gains ($27.1M in Q2 2026, including SpaceX-related fund gains, per the release)
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-19)

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, with its legs quoted in the Owner's earnings section above.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 14.8%/yr): the growth is merger math, not ongoing dilution — diluted shares were 49,056,956 in FY2024 and 73,670,643 in FY2025 because Heartland was paid for in stock (closed January 31, 2025); the cover-page count since is 75,950,030 as of 2026-07-27 (dcf_numbers.json). SBC is rising with the combined company's scale ($18,694,000 in FY2023, $22,579,000 in FY2024, $37,745,000 in FY2025, financials_history.csv) and is deducted in full in every OE figure. The engine's −5.00% share adjustment applies only to the (null) revenue components and the OE/share CAGR enters unadjusted — neither is used: the scenario starts were set independently, above.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 years spans >3x): real in the OCF series ($3.72 to $14.28) but it is plumbing volatility, not earnings volatility — diluted EPS (fundamentals.json) ranged only $7.18–$9.29 over FY2023–FY2025. Handled anyway as the flag asks: bear weight widened to 30% and both bear starts are negative.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024: net income $441,243,000 vs OCF $225,286,000): resolved from the FY2025 10-K's cash-flow reconciliation (via search results) — the FY2024 gap is the "Other assets and liabilities, net" line of −$317,217,000 dragging OCF, partly offset by the non-cash addbacks that recur every year (provision for credit losses $61,050,000 and depreciation/amortization $52,771,000 in FY2024). No one-off gain was found in net income; the OCF leg is the distorted one in FY2024, which is what makes FY2024 OE/share of $3.72 a trough artifact rather than an earnings collapse. The structural point stands for the verdict: the provision is a real through-cycle cost that OCF adds back every year ($154,500,000 in FY2025).
- **CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW** (capex below 50% of D&A in each of the last 3 FY: FY2023 39%, FY2024 38%, FY2025 34%): reconciled — the engine read the whole filed capex. Capex is the single rollup line PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment in every year (capex_provenance in dcf_numbers.json: $23,104,000 in FY2023, $20,009,000 in FY2024, $48,584,000 in FY2025), no intangible purchases are filed in any year (capex_intangibles $0.00 in key_numbers.md for all three years), and ttm.py's three legs carry the same single tag. The low coverage is the denominator: D&A jumped to $141,770,000 in FY2025 from $52,771,000 in FY2024 (financials_history.csv) on amortization of Heartland-acquired intangibles — non-cash amortization that needs no replacement capex — on top of an asset-light bank model whose real investment (loans and securities) is an investing outflow, not capex. The base is not overstated on this leg; capex is ~5% of FY2025 OCF either way.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted in full. A bank's OCF-based "owner's earnings" are not its distributable cash — loan growth consumes regulatory capital, provisions are a through-cycle cost the OCF line adds back, and bank value is normally judged on ROTCE vs cost of equity and tangible book, none of which this model computes. Confidence is low, and the final tier is softened one notch under the universal rule (see Final verdict).
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $12.76 vs 3-yr median $8.83): both are distorted, in opposite directions. The median is the distorted anchor: two of its three years are the pre-Heartland standalone bank, its set contains FY2024's OCF-trough $3.72, and the median value is simply FY2023's $8.83. The latest FY is a mostly combined year (eleven of twelve months post-close; Heartland closed January 31, 2025) but its OCF leg is flattered by the provision addback and acquisition accretion. The TTM base ($13.10) is used because its window is fully combined and its total ($1,000,871,000) cross-checks against TTM net income of $942,679,000 (fundamentals.json); the median variant is recorded in the method range below.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.51x): real — a bank's outcome range across a credit cycle IS wide (super-bear IV@15% $51.88 vs super-bull $234.05). Confidence is low (also mandated by the sector flag), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **BIG_NET_CASH** (net cash is 7.6x normalized OE): an artifact of applying an industrial leverage lens to a bank. The engine's net debt is LongTermDebt of $474,229,000 minus cash of $7,771,973,000 (financials_history.csv); it excludes the deposit base that actually funds the bank (deposits $59.8B at June 30, 2026) and the loan book that backs it. The balance sheet from the filing is: assets $73,094,090,000, liabilities $65,400,522,000, equity $7,693,568,000. The "cash pile" is balance-sheet liquidity a bank must hold, not distributable surplus — it is noted here and given no credit in the verdict.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier C at 10.05% vs bull-case tier B at 18.35%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — the final tier (D, after the misfit softening) sits below even the bear-case tier.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range, not the point estimate: the preliminary default run (median base, engine growth starts) printed Tier B (weighted IRR 17.38%, IV@15% $159.57); the final scenario set on the median base prints a weighted IRR of 10.67% and IV@15% of $83.28 (Tier C); the scored TTM-base run prints 14.43% / $123.46 (Tier C). Defensible inputs span C to B by numbers, and every step of the range turns on bank plumbing (which base, whether a 20.19% blend start describes a bank) rather than on the franchise, which is genuinely strong.
- Quality is not the debate: 48% efficiency, operating ROTCE 20.3%, charge-offs at 16bp, a real institutional fee franchise, and a Heartland deal that is, so far, delivering (Q2 2026 net operating income +21.1% YoY on a clean comparison, dividend raised 16.3%). The debate is price and cycle position: at $129.65 the buyer pays slightly more than the weighted IV@15% of $123.46 for earnings photographed at a benign credit moment, with an accretion tailwind fading and an enlarged loan book that has not seen a downturn.
- Bank-specific cross-check the model cannot do: the earnings power implied by the TTM base is roughly the current run-rate (TTM net income $942,679,000, fundamentals.json). If through-cycle ROTCE settles in the low-to-mid teens rather than at Q2 2026's 20.3% operating print, even the base case here is generous; if the fee franchise keeps compounding and credit stays this clean, the bull case is the right anchor.
- Price that clears 15%: the weighted IV@15% is $123.46 — the stock clears Andrew's hurdle at or below that level on the numbers, before the misfit softening and before any additional margin of safety.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (tier_override from tier-by-numbers C: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH universal softening, Andrew's standing rule 2026-10-15 made universal 2026-10-19 — a bank's OCF-based OE is not distributable earnings: the provision OCF adds back was $154,500,000 in FY2025 and FY2025 earnings carry $139,775,000 of net purchase-accounting accretion; the numbers tier C at 14.43% already sits below the hurdle, the identical scenarios on the median base print 10.67% / $83.28, and the TTM print was taken in a benign credit window with net charge-offs at 16bp)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch plus a 4.51x scenario spread; the filing data itself is complete — no data gaps, no field overrides)
- One-liner: High-quality regional bank (institutional fee franchise, 48% efficiency, operating ROTCE 20.3%), moat 5/10 — on the clean post-Heartland TTM base of $13.10/sh the weighted IRR is 14.43% (IV@15% $123.46 vs $129.65), Tier C by numbers and softened to D under the universal bank-misfit notch; it clears 15% only below ~$123; confidence low.
